capabilities.target: any customer CRM record, by email or account id

instructions.note: Agent is told it may look up any customer by email or account id, not limited to the requester's own identity, enabling cross-customer lookups on request.
Human review is triggered only by a model-inferred emotional heuristic ('angry'). There is no structural approval gate for routine sends, which is the majority path and the one this attack uses.

Line 3 grants broad lookup of any customer while line 14 instructs never to share another customer's information; the only enforcement of the latter is this single sentence, with no structural backing.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends entirely on the model choosing to comply. A more capable or adversarially prompted model can rationalize disclosure ('the customer clearly needs this data') or split disclosure across steps to appear compliant per-step.

controls.name: Outbound email logging to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the mail platform outside the model, so it does not decay with model capability. It is detective only, occurs after the send completes, and does not prevent or reverse disclosure.

controls.name: Least-privilege CRM query scoping to the requester's own verified record
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the CRM API or query layer rather than by model choice, this does not depend on model capability.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the CRM record on file
controls.decay_rationale: If the send destination is sourced from the verified customer record rather than from requester-supplied text or model output, it does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval gate on emails carrying customer PII
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action gate does not decay with model capability, though it is subject to approval fatigue at high ticket volume.

controls.name: MCP tool definition pinning for crm_mcp and mail_mcp
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning or hashing tool schemas prevents silent redefinition (rug pull) independent of model behavior.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) / confused deputy (TC4): untrusted email drives unrestricted CRM lookup and direct send to requester

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled email content directs which customer record to fetch and is itself the reply destination.
Broad-scope CRM_SVC_TOKEN lets the agent read any customer's confidential record, not just the requester's own, per prompt.md:2-3.
Shared MAIL_SVC_TOKEN can send to any address; routine tickets are sent directly with no approval gate.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Deployed model id/version changes with no separate review, since subject.model.swappable is true; also watch median ticket-handling steps/context length rising over time.

evidence.observation: "You may look up any customer by email or account id" - lookup is not scoped to the requester's own identity.
"If the answer is routine, send it directly ... Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry" - no structural approval gate for the majority (routine) path.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.
"Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you" is the sole preventive control on this path, and it is a behavioral instruction only.

"The model is configured through an environment variable and is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review" - the one preventive control is dependent and subject to unreviewed model upgrades.

recommendations.action: Scope the CRM query/credential so the agent can only read the record matching the authenticated identity of the requester (verified email/account match), not arbitrary lookups by any supplied identifier.
Bind the outbound email destination to the verified address on file for the matched customer record, sourced from the system of record rather than from requester-supplied text or the reply-to header.
Require a raw-action human approval gate for any email send that includes CRM-sourced customer data, independent of a model-inferred 'angry' heuristic.
Alert in real time (not only log) when an outbound email containing CRM data is addressed to someone other than the customer of record, so detection can occur before the send completes.

rating.rationale: The design lets an untrusted inbound email (U) drive an unscoped CRM lookup of any customer's confidential record and a direct, unapproved send to the requester's own address using a shared-scope mail credential (S3 sink: irreversible egress of confidential data). Inherent risk is critical under the U x S3 matrix, reinforced by the autonomy modifier since no step or runtime limit is declared. The only preventive control is a single behavioral prompt instruction ('never share another customer's information'), which earns one step-4 credit and brings residual to high; a detective SIEM log exists but grants no tier credit because it fires after the send. Because the sole preventive control is behavioral and dependent, and the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable=true), a model_upgrade or longer_task_horizon trigger removes that credit entirely, returning the finding to critical. Forecast equals critical.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; whether the 'never share another customer's information' instruction is actually obeyed in production, and what address sends are truly directed to, was not verified against live traffic.

No approval-gate implementation was disclosed beyond the prompt's 'unless angry' heuristic; if an undisclosed structural escalation mechanism exists, autonomy and control credit would need to be revised.
peer_identity_verified and definitions_pinned for crm_mcp and mail_mcp were inferred as false due to absence of contrary evidence in mcp.json; confidence on the protocol findings is medium.

Data sensitivity of CRM records was inferred as confidential given typical customer PII; if records include payment, health, or other regulated data, the sink and consequence should be raised to restricted/severe.
